text:
anna: Quick heads-up — I'm seeing a regression in our mixed-model co-residency perf tests after the kernel-selector change. p50 up ~18% on the night run (same batch shapes). Anyone else seeing this?
perf-bot: nightly-bench: mixed-A+B (64batches) p50: 86ms -> 102ms (+18%) p95: 210ms -> 236ms (+12%); GPU mem HWM unchanged; swap_count +14% (see /ci/artifacts/176350/bench-summary.txt)
leo: Do we have KV cache hit-rate diffs for the same run? That would explain the extra token latency if more misses -> regen.
anna: got KV dump from the run: hit-rate went 78% -> 64%. Misses cluster on model B eviction windows. Quick snapshot: `kv_hits: 6400, kv_misses: 3600` (per 10k requests).
maria: probably due to kernel-selector preferring the new fused attention kernel. It allocates a larger ephemeral workspace for the same sequence length (we saw +256KB per workspace), which increases fragmentation and forces earlier KV swaps on multi-model packs. Allocator logs show repeated small free fragments: `slab:free 32k 24k 48k 16k ...`
shawn: ugh. If the workspace footprint per request rises, small models lose their hot KV pages first. Two ideas: 1) revert kernel selector heuristics; 2) try a soft isolation scheme that lets tiny models borrow a transient slot to keep their KV resident — call it "slot-lending" for now.
kai: slot-lending sounds promising. Prototype config I ran locally: `--allocator.soft_partitions=1 --allocator.slot_lend_fraction=0.15 --allocator.prefetch_baton=2`. It temporarily pins a small shadow-slot for borrowers and prefetches KV pages just before kernel dispatch.
infra-oncall: careful with any lending/overcommit on prod Dedicated pools — affects isolation SLAs. Can we canary this on a non-SLA pool first?
anna: agreed on canary. I ran a small simulator with slot-lending enabled on the mixed A+B trace: p50 improved from 102ms -> 94ms (partial recovery), kv_hit up to 71%, but fragmentation metric (free-run-length entropy) got worse. Short numbers from the sim: `p50:94ms p95:222ms kv_hit:71% swap_count:-6% frag_score:+18%`
maria: we should dig into buffer reuse patterns. The allocator's coalescing path seems less effective when fused kernels allocate and free many small temp buffers inside a request. If we can promote those temps to a thread-local reuse-cache instead of returning to global slabs, we reduce the global fragmentation spike.
leo: I can add a lightweight memory profiler to the runtime that emits per-request histogram of alloc sizes and alloc/free hot spots. Will tag the logs with model id and kernel variant. Any constraints?
anna: please do. Add these fields: `model_id`, `kernel_variant`, `alloc_sequence` and KV eviction reason. Post to S3 and ping perf-bot when done.
leo: starting now. ETA ~2h.
shawn: also: kernel-selector should expose the estimated workspace delta in the decision path so the router can consider workspace delta when co-scheduling models. Right now it only considers FLOPs and latency. That might avoid pairing two workspace-heavy models.
kai: quick config diff I ran to test prefetching + lending: ```diff
- allocator.soft_partitions = false
+ allocator.soft_partitions = true
+ allocator.slot_lend_fraction = 0.12
+ allocator.prefetch_baton = 3
+ allocator.reuse_thread_cache = true
``` This lowered swap churn in my local sim.
perf-bot: adhoc-run 1763505020: mixed-A+B with slot-lend+reuse-thread-cache: p50 92ms (-9% vs broken), p95 218ms (-7%); kv_hit 73% (+9pts), swap_count -11%
maria: promising. Next we need to stress test long traces (1M requests) to check compaction/regression over time. If reuse cache grows unbounded we could see worse HWM later. Also need to verify no cross-tenant leakage.
infra-oncall: canary plan: three stages — dev pool, non-SLA dedicated pool, then controlled rollout to SLA pools behind a feature flag. Add explicit kill-switch env var.
anna: agreed. Action items: 1) leo — ship profiler and the tagged logs (ETA 2h). 2) kai — create canary config and run 1M-request sim with compaction enabled (ETA EOD). 3) shawn/maria — draft rollout + metrics dashboard (kv_hit, swap_count, p50_by_model, frag_score, slot_lend_usage, isolation_violations). 4) infra-oncall — reserve a non-SLA dedicated pool for canary.
leo: I'll @perf-bot to post results to #eng-runtime when done.
shawn: one more note — we should add a kernel-selector unit test that asserts workspace_delta <= threshold when co-scheduling heavy models. Prevents regressions like this.
anna: +1. Thanks everyone. Let's keep the changes behind a feature flag until metrics are stable. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: scheduled follow-up benchmark in 3h (/ci/jobs/176350/slot-lend-smoke). Will post summary when complete.
anna: if the smoke looks good, we can canary tomorrow morning.
